indications.ageWarningText: For neonates (<28d), use 10–15 mg/kg/dose q6–8h (max 60 mg/kg/day).
indications.clinicalPearls: Max 5 doses/24h (75 mg/kg/day up to 4000 mg/day). Verify concentration: infant & children's liquids in the US are standardized to 160 mg/5 mL.
indications.name: Fever / Pain (Oral)

indications.clinicalPearls: Rectal absorption is slower and more variable than oral; avoid splitting suppositories if possible due to uneven drug distribution.
indications.name: Fever / Pain (Rectal)

indications.clinicalPearls: Infuse over 15 minutes. In infants <2 years, consider 7.5–12.5 mg/kg/dose q6h per institutional protocol.
indications.name: Moderate Pain / Fever (IV)

summary: First-line antipyretic & mild-to-moderate analgesic (PO/PR/IV).

indications.clinicalPearls: 20 mg/kg/dose IV q8h is standard for neonatal HSV and pediatric HSV encephalitis (<12y).
indications.name: HSV Encephalitis / Neonatal HSV (IV)
indications.renalNote: Ensure adequate IV hydration to prevent crystal nephropathy; adjust in renal impairment.

indications.clinicalPearls: Start within 24 hours of rash onset for varicella in immunocompromised or ≥12y patients.
indications.name: Varicella / Mucocutaneous HSV (PO)

summary: Antiviral for HSV encephalitis, neonatal HSV, and severe varicella.

indications.clinicalPearls: Use 3-way stopcock with 5–10 mL NS flush in proximal vein. If no conversion after 1–2 min, give 2nd dose of 0.2 mg/kg (max 12 mg).
indications.frequencyLabel: rapid IV push + immediate NS flush
indications.name: SVT — 1st Dose (Rapid IV Push)

indications.clinicalPearls: Keep continuous ECG rhythm strip running during administration.
indications.frequencyLabel: rapid IV push + immediate NS flush
indications.name: SVT — 2nd Dose (Rapid IV Push)

summary: PALS antiarrhythmic for Supraventricular Tachycardia (SVT).

indications.clinicalPearls: Minimum practical neb dose is 2.5 mg (3 mL of 0.083% nebules) for <20 kg, and 5 mg for ≥20 kg in most ED pathways.
indications.name: Acute Asthma Exacerbation (Nebulizer)

summary: Short-acting beta-2 agonist (SABA) for acute bronchospasm / asthma.

indications.clinicalPearls: Give as rapid bolus in cardiac arrest. For perfusing tachyarrhythmias, infuse slowly over 20–60 min to avoid hypotension.
indications.frequencyLabel: IV/IO bolus; may repeat up to 3 total doses
indications.name: Pulseless VF / pVT (Refractory)

summary: PALS Class III antiarrhythmic for shock-refractory VF/pVT.

indications.clinicalPearls: 90 mg/kg/day divided BID overcomes penicillin-non-susceptible S. pneumoniae. Max 1000 mg/dose (or 2000 mg/day in many outpatient AOM guidelines).
indications.name: Acute Otitis Media / CAP (High-Dose)

indications.clinicalPearls: Once-daily 50 mg/kg (max 1000 mg) x 10 days is AAP first-line for Group A Strep pharyngitis.
indications.name: GAS Pharyngitis (Standard)

summary: First-line aminopenicillin for AOM, strep pharyngitis, and CAP.

indications.clinicalPearls: Use 600 mg/42.9 mg per 5 mL (14:1 ratio) for 90 mg/kg/day to minimize clavulanate-induced diarrhea.
indications.name: Recurrent AOM / Sinusitis (ES-600 High-Dose)

indications.clinicalPearls: Use 400 mg/57 mg per 5 mL or 200 mg/28.5 mg per 5 mL suspension for BID standard dosing.
indications.name: Skin / Bite / UTI (Standard)

summary: Beta-lactam/beta-lactamase inhibitor (dosed by amoxicillin component).

indications.clinicalPearls: PALS minimum single dose (0.1 mg) was removed in recent updates for infants, though many centers still observe 0.1 mg floor. Max child single dose 0.5 mg (1 mg adolescent).
indications.frequencyLabel: once; may repeat once in 5 min
indications.name: Symptomatic Bradycardia (Vagal / AV Block)

summary: Anticholinergic for symptomatic vagal bradycardia & organophosphate toxicity.

indications.clinicalPearls: Days 2–5: 5 mg/kg once daily (max 250 mg). For pertussis in infants <6m, 10 mg/kg/day x 5 days (monitor for IHPS in <1m).
indications.name: Atypical CAP / Pertussis (Day 1)

indications.clinicalPearls: Follows Day 1 loading dose of 10 mg/kg (max 500 mg).
indications.name: Atypical CAP (Days 2–5)

indications.clinicalPearls: Higher macrolide resistance in GAS; reserve for true severe penicillin allergy.
indications.name: GAS Pharyngitis (PCN Allergy)

summary: Macrolide for atypical pneumonia, pertussis, and penicillin-allergic pharyngitis.

indications.clinicalPearls: 10% Calcium Gluconate = 100 mg/mL (so 100 mg/kg = 1 mL/kg). Never mix with sodium bicarbonate or ceftriaxone in the same line.
indications.frequencyLabel: slow IV over 5–10 min w/ ECG monitoring
indications.name: Hyperkalemia / Symptomatic Hypocalcemia

summary: Membrane stabilizer for hyperkalemia, hypocalcemia, and CCB toxicity.

indications.clinicalPearls: Surgical prophylaxis: 30 mg/kg IV (max 2000 mg) within 60 min prior to incision.
indications.name: MSSA / Moderate-Severe Infection

summary: IV 1st-gen cephalosporin for MSSA bacteremia, SSTI, and surgical prophylaxis.

indications.clinicalPearls: Can cause harmless reddish stools when co-administered with iron-containing formula/supplements.
indications.name: AOM / Sinusitis / UTI

summary: 3rd-generation oral cephalosporin for AOM, sinusitis, and UTI.

formulations.label: 100 mg / mL IV Soln (1 g/10 mL)

indications.ageWarningText: CONTRAINDICATED in hyperbilirubinemic neonates & premature neonates; avoid <28d (use Cefotaxime/Cefepime) and never co-administer with IV calcium.
indications.clinicalPearls: For IM AOM: 50 mg/kg x 1 (or x 3 days for treatment failure), max 1000 mg.
indications.name: Sepsis / Pneumonia / Pyelonephritis / AOM (IM)

indications.ageWarningText: Avoid in neonates ≤28 days; use Cefotaxime or Cefepime + Ampicillin.
indications.clinicalPearls: Often paired with Vancomycin empirically until CSF cultures/susceptibilities return.
indications.name: Bacterial Meningitis

indications.clinicalPearls: Reconstitute with 1% Lidocaine (without epinephrine) for IM injection ONLY — never administer Lidocaine-reconstituted ceftriaxone IV.
indications.name: Refractory Acute Otitis Media (IM)

summary: Broad-spectrum IV/IM 3rd-gen cephalosporin for serious bacterial infections.

indications.clinicalPearls: For severe MSSA osteomyelitis or deep SSTI, doses up to 75–100 mg/kg/day (max 4000 mg/day) are used.
indications.name: Cellulitis / UTI (Standard)

summary: 1st-generation cephalosporin for MSSA skin/soft tissue infections & UTI.

indications.clinicalPearls: Standard age tiers: 6m–2y: 2.5 mg daily; 2–5y: 2.5–5 mg daily; ≥6y: 5–10 mg daily.
indications.frequencyLabel: once daily (or divided BID for urticaria)
indications.name: Allergic Rhinitis / Urticaria

summary: 2nd-generation minimally sedating antihistamine for urticaria & allergic rhinitis.

indications.clinicalPearls: Oral solution is notoriously bitter; warn caregivers. Monitor for C. difficile diarrhea.
indications.name: SSTI / MRSA / Odontogenic (PO)

indications.clinicalPearls: Infuse over 10–60 min; rapid IV push can cause hypotension/cardiac arrest.
indications.name: Severe SSTI / Deep Neck / Toxic Shock (IV)

summary: Lincosamide for MRSA skin infections, odontogenic, and anaerobic infections.

indications.clinicalPearls: 0.6 mg/kg PO/IM/IV (max 16 mg; some asthma protocols cap at 12 mg). IV formulation (4 mg/mL or 10 mg/mL) can be given PO mixed with flavoring.
indications.name: Croup / Acute Asthma Exacerbation

indications.clinicalPearls: Give 10–20 min before or simultaneously with first antibiotic dose for suspected H. influenzae or S. pneumoniae meningitis.
indications.name: Bacterial Meningitis Adjunct

summary: Long-acting corticosteroid for croup, asthma exacerbation, and meningitis.

indications.clinicalPearls: Neonates: 2 mL/kg D10W (0.2 g/kg). Infants/children: 2–5 mL/kg D10W (0.2–0.5 g/kg). D10W is preferred over D50W in pediatrics to reduce extravasation necrosis.
indications.frequencyLabel: slow IV push; recheck glucose in 15 min
indications.name: Hypoglycemia (Neonates & Children)

summary: First-line IV dextrose for pediatric & neonatal hypoglycemia.

indications.ageWarningText: Avoid OTC use in children <2 years; use with caution <6 years due to sedation/paradoxical excitation.
indications.clinicalPearls: Do NOT use as monotherapy for anaphylaxis — Epinephrine IM is first-line.
indications.name: Acute Allergic Reaction / Urticaria (PO)

indications.ageWarningText: Avoid in <2 years unless emergent dystonia/anaphylaxis adjunct under close monitoring.
indications.clinicalPearls: Administer IV slowly (max 25 mg/min).
indications.name: Acute Allergic Reaction / Dystonia (IV/IM)

summary: 1st-generation H1 antihistamine for acute urticaria, allergic reactions, and dystonia.

indications.clinicalPearls: 0.01 mg/kg (= 0.01 mL/kg of 1 mg/mL [1:1,000]). Max 0.3 mg in prepubertal children, 0.5 mg in adolescents/adults. Auto-injectors: 0.1 mg (7.5–15 kg), 0.15 mg (15–30 kg), 0.3 mg (≥30 kg).
indications.name: Anaphylaxis (Anterolateral Thigh IM)

summary: First-line IM treatment for anaphylaxis (1 mg/mL = 1:1,000).

indications.clinicalPearls: 0.01 mg/kg (= 0.1 mL/kg of 0.1 mg/mL [1:10,000]). Follow with 5 mL NS flush. ETT dose (if no IV/IO): 0.1 mg/kg (0.1 mL/kg of 1:1,000).
indications.name: Cardiac Arrest / Symptomatic Bradycardia

summary: PALS resuscitation dose (0.1 mg/mL = 1:10,000).

indications.clinicalPearls: Give before meals or at bedtime.
indications.name: GERD / Acid Suppression (PO)
indications.renalNote: Reduce dose by 50% if CrCl <50 mL/min.

indications.clinicalPearls: H2 blocker adjunct in anaphylaxis (after IM Epinephrine).
indications.name: GERD / Anaphylaxis Adjunct (IV)
indications.renalNote: Reduce dose by 50% if CrCl <50 mL/min.

summary: H2 receptor antagonist for GERD, gastritis, and anaphylaxis adjunct.

indications.clinicalPearls: Rapid IV push can cause chest wall rigidity. Intranasal route often uses 1.5–2 mcg/kg (max 100 mcg).
indications.name: Acute / Procedural Pain (IV)

summary: Rapid-onset short-acting opioid for procedural/acute severe pain.

indications.clinicalPearls: Invasive candidiasis uses 12 mg/kg/dose (max 800 mg) IV/PO daily.
indications.name: Oropharyngeal / Esophageal Candidiasis

summary: Triazole antifungal for candidiasis.

formulations.label: 50 mg / mL IV Vial (100 mg/2 mL)

indications.clinicalPearls: BSA-based stress dose is 50–100 mg/m² IV bolus followed by 50–100 mg/m²/day divided q6h. Check glucose and electrolytes.
indications.name: Adrenal Crisis / Refractory Shock (Stress Dose)

summary: Stress-dose glucocorticoid for adrenal crisis / catecholamine-refractory shock.

indications.clinicalPearls: Sedating; avoid in patients with prolonged QTc.
indications.name: Pruritus / Urticaria

summary: Antihistamine for pruritus and chronic urticaria.

indications.ageWarningText: Avoid in infants <6 months (renal/GI toxicity risk).
indications.clinicalPearls: Give with food if GI upset occurs. Max 400 mg/dose for fever/pain (600–800 mg/dose reserved for JIA/adult). Note Infant Drops (50 mg/1.25 mL) vs Children's Suspension (100 mg/5 mL).
indications.name: Fever / Analgesia
indications.renalNote: Avoid in dehydration, AKI, or significant renal impairment.

summary: NSAID antipyretic, analgesic, and anti-inflammatory (≥6 months).

indications.clinicalPearls: 250 mcg (0.25 mg) for <20 kg or <12y in some protocols; 500 mcg (0.5 mg) for ≥20 kg. Mix directly with albuterol.
indications.name: Moderate-Severe Asthma Adjunct (Neb)

summary: Anticholinergic bronchodilator adjunct for moderate-severe acute asthma.

indications.clinicalPearls: Max 15 mg/dose in many pediatric IV protocols for children <50 kg (30 mg for ≥50 kg). Limit total duration to ≤5 days.
indications.name: Acute Pain (IV/IM)
indications.renalNote: Contraindicated in renal insufficiency, dehydration, or active bleeding.

summary: Potent parenteral NSAID for acute moderate-to-severe pain.

indications.clinicalPearls: ESETT trial validated 60 mg/kg (max 4500 mg) IV over 10 min as equally effective to fosphenytoin/valproate with fewer hemodynamic side effects.
indications.name: Status Epilepticus (2nd-Line IV Load)

indications.clinicalPearls: Typically initiated at 10 mg/kg/dose PO BID and titrated every 2 weeks up to 30 mg/kg/dose BID.
indications.name: Seizure Maintenance (PO)
indications.renalNote: Adjust dose in moderate-to-severe renal impairment.

summary: Second-line anti-seizure medication for benzodiazepine-refractory status epilepticus.

indications.clinicalPearls: Monitor respiratory status and SpO2 closely. Have bag-valve-mask ready.
indications.frequencyLabel: over 1–2 min; may repeat x 1 in 5–10 min
indications.name: Status Epilepticus (IV/IO)

summary: First-line IV/IO benzodiazepine for status epilepticus.

indications.clinicalPearls: Max initial bolus 60–80 mg. Transition to oral prednisolone/dexamethasone once tolerating PO.
indications.name: Status Asthmaticus (Load then Maintenance)

summary: IV corticosteroid for status asthmaticus and severe inflammation.

indications.clinicalPearls: Giardiasis typically uses 15 mg/kg/day divided TID x 5–7 days.
indications.name: Anaerobic / C. difficile Infection

summary: Nitroimidazole for anaerobic infections, C. difficile, and giardiasis.

indications.clinicalPearls: Ideal when IV access is not yet established. For IN, use 5 mg/mL concentration and split between nares (max 1 mL/nostril).
indications.name: Status Epilepticus (IM or Intranasal)

indications.clinicalPearls: Monitor airway and ventilation continuously.
indications.name: Status Epilepticus / Sedation (IV)

summary: Rapid-acting benzodiazepine for IM/IN/IV status epilepticus & sedation.

indications.ageWarningText: Neonates/young infants: start at 0.025–0.05 mg/kg/dose; monitor for apnea.
indications.clinicalPearls: Administer slowly over 3–5 minutes. Have naloxone available and monitor SpO2/respiratory rate.
indications.name: Severe Pain (IV)
indications.renalNote: Accumulates active M6G metabolite in renal impairment.

indications.clinicalPearls: Oral bioavailability is ~30% of IV. Titrate carefully.
indications.name: Severe Pain (Oral)

summary: Opioid analgesic for severe acute pain.

indications.clinicalPearls: For iatrogenic post-op oversedation (non-overdose), titrate small doses of 0.001–0.01 mg/kg to avoid acute withdrawal/pain.
indications.name: Opioid Overdose / Apnea Reversal

summary: Opioid receptor antagonist for respiratory depression / overdose.

indications.ageWarningText: Avoid in neonates <1 month (hemolytic anemia risk).
indications.clinicalPearls: Does NOT achieve therapeutic renal parenchymal or serum levels — never use for febrile UTI/pyelonephritis.
indications.name: Uncomplicated Cystitis (Not Pyelonephritis)

summary: Urinary-tract-specific antibiotic for uncomplicated cystitis (≥1 month).

indications.clinicalPearls: Use 10 mL/kg boluses in neonates, DKA, or suspected cardiogenic shock / myocarditis. Reassess perfusion, lung crackles, and hepatomegaly after each bolus.
indications.frequencyLabel: over 5–20 min; reassess after each bolus
indications.name: Hypovolemic / Septic Shock Bolus

summary: Isotonic crystalloid fluid resuscitation bolus.

indications.clinicalPearls: Give 30–60 min before first meal of the day for optimal parietal cell proton pump inhibition.
indications.name: GERD / Erosive Esophagitis

summary: Proton pump inhibitor (PPI) for erosive esophagitis and severe GERD.

indications.clinicalPearls: Standard ED weight tiers: 8–15 kg = 2 mg ODT; 15–30 kg = 4 mg ODT; >30 kg = 8 mg ODT. Caution in congenital long QT syndrome.
indications.name: Nausea / Vomiting (Oral)

indications.clinicalPearls: 4 mg max per IV dose for post-op nausea/vomiting in most pediatric protocols.
indications.name: Nausea / Vomiting (IV)

summary: 5-HT3 antagonist antiemetic for acute gastroenteritis & post-op nausea.

indications.clinicalPearls: 3 mg/kg/dose BID is for infants <12 months. For ≥1 year, select the weight-tier indication.
indications.name: Influenza Treatment (<12 months)

indications.clinicalPearls: CDC/AAP weight-band dosing for ≥1 year and ≤15 kg: 30 mg PO BID x 5 days.
indications.name: Influenza ≥1y (≤15 kg Tier)

indications.clinicalPearls: CDC/AAP weight-band dosing for ≥1 year and >15–23 kg: 45 mg PO BID x 5 days.
indications.name: Influenza ≥1y (>15–23 kg Tier)

indications.clinicalPearls: CDC/AAP weight-band dosing for ≥1 year and >23–40 kg: 60 mg PO BID x 5 days.
indications.name: Influenza ≥1y (>23–40 kg Tier)

indications.clinicalPearls: CDC/AAP weight-band dosing for ≥1 year and >40 kg: 75 mg PO BID x 5 days.
indications.name: Influenza ≥1y (>40 kg Tier)

summary: Neuraminidase inhibitor for Influenza A/B treatment and prophylaxis.

indications.clinicalPearls: Use lowest effective dose for shortest duration. Verify concentration (5 mg/5 mL vs 20 mg/mL concentrate).
indications.name: Moderate-Severe Pain (PO)

summary: Oral opioid analgesic for moderate-to-severe acute pain.

indications.clinicalPearls: If seizures persist after 20 mg/kg, may give additional 10–20 mg/kg (up to 40 mg/kg total load) with close respiratory/BP monitoring.
indications.name: Neonatal / Refractory Seizures (IV Load)

summary: First-line anti-seizure medication for neonatal seizures.

indications.clinicalPearls: 1 capful = 17 g (17,000 mg). Mix in 4–8 oz of water or juice. Disimpaction uses 1–1.5 g/kg/day x 3–6 days.
indications.name: Maintenance Constipation

summary: Osmotic laxative for functional constipation and fecal disimpaction.

indications.clinicalPearls: 1–2 mg/kg/day (max 60 mg/day). Give with food. Concentrates like 15 mg/5 mL reduce total volume for young children.
indications.name: Asthma Exacerbation (Burst)

summary: Oral corticosteroid for asthma exacerbations and inflammatory conditions.

indications.clinicalPearls: 0.05 mL/kg of 2.25% solution (max 0.5 mL) diluted in 3 mL NS. Observe for 2–4h post-dose for rebound stridor; always pair with Dexamethasone.
indications.name: Croup (Stridor at Rest)

summary: Nebulized alpha/beta agonist for moderate-to-severe croup stridor.

indications.clinicalPearls: 1 mEq/mL = 8.4% solution (standard pediatric/adult). In neonates, dilute 1:1 with sterile water (0.5 mEq/mL = 4.2%) to reduce osmolarity.
indications.name: TCA Toxicity / Severe Acidosis (1 mEq/mL)

summary: Alkalinizing agent for TCA overdose, severe hyperkalemia, and metabolic acidosis.

indications.clinicalPearls: Dosed based on Trimethoprim (TMP) component. 5 mL of suspension = 40 mg TMP / 200 mg SMX. 1 DS tablet = 160 mg TMP.
indications.name: UTI / Purulent SSTI (MRSA)

summary: Sulfonamide/DHFR inhibitor for UTI and purulent MRSA SSTI (dosed by TMP).

indications.clinicalPearls: Infuse over ≥60 min (max 10 mg/min) to prevent Vancomycin Infusion Reaction (flushing/histamine release).
indications.name: Systemic MRSA / Sepsis / Meningitis
indications.renalNote: Requires AUC/trough TDM and renal adjustment.

summary: Glycopeptide for serious MRSA, resistant Gram-positive, and meningitis.
